content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods (e.g., first 5–10 days) and overestimates in late periods (e.g., last 5–10 days), suggesting a lag or delayed response to trend changes.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 60→70+), then fails to correct — model overreacts and overcorrects.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained upward trends.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon show persistent underestimation of upward momentum, especially in late cycle (e.g., 65–75 range).
- Model exhibits “early dip” bias — underpredicts initial price drops, then overpredicts recovery.
- High variance in forecast error near 60–70 range — model struggles to capture volatility in mid-range price zones.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or policy-driven spikes (e.g., March 2024: policy-driven price jumps not captured early).
